governing_intent: Implement the deterministic, I/O-free Execution Coordination domain kernel that owns released-BIU admission, lifecycle policy, scheduling, custody gating, verdict admissibility, and the BIU contract model.
summary: PY-02 is bounded, coherent, and executable within approved authority. It deliberately implements pure policy only; durability, adapters, runtime invocation, and operational integration remain assigned to later BIUs.
implementation_unknowns: Choose concrete immutable Python value types, typed error/result shapes, canonical serialization, and digest algorithm.
Define precise pure-function APIs and table-driven fixtures for contract validation, admission, lifecycle transitions, scheduling, and verdict evaluation.
Extend the existing AST fitness checker with an appropriately scoped detection set for direct clock, randomness, and identifier-generation imports.
verification_assessment: Real executable proof is specified: deterministic unit/table tests cover each acceptance rule; fitness must fail on deliberate violating fixtures and pass on the actual tree with preserved nonzero status; existing PY-01 fitness checks and the Node suite must also pass. The current PY-01 fitness harness already demonstrates the required fixture-versus-tree pattern and is a suitable extension point.
material_risks: The contract’s readiness link points to PY-02.assessment.json, while the Wave 1 plan describes a PY-0N.request.md to PY-0N.assessment.json flow; this is documentation-path hygiene, not an implementation or authority blocker.

The exact Python representation and canonical digest serialization must be selected deterministically, but those are delegated engineering details constrained by the immutable, content-addressed contract requirement.

Lifecycle closure actions must remain contract-provided data and policy evaluation, without prematurely implementing persistence, external publication, or worker/runtime mechanics assigned to later BIUs.
next_action: Record this READY assessment, then move PY-02 through the authorized TASKS-to-READY workflow; do not begin implementation until separately authorized.
rationale: Founder-approved authority fixes the ownership boundary, lifecycle vocabulary, release ON/OFF policy, budget fail-closed behavior, concurrency direction, candidate-custody invariant, Python module boundary, and Node coexistence constraints. The pre-Python reclassification explicitly identifies remaining API, schema, and fitness-rule detail as normal implementation work and found zero unresolved Founder-level decisions. PY-02’s scope, non-goals, requirement extents, dependency, and mechanical acceptance criteria align with the approved Wave 1 DAG without creating a second decision center.
